study type: Secondary analysis of a prospective observational study
exposure: SGA neonates born to obese mothers
SGA neonates born to non-obese mothers
cohort: Women undergoing repeat cesarean delivery at or after 37 weeks gestation, excluding multiple gestations, fetal anomalies, >1 prior CD, and medical diseases
finding: While SGA was associated with higher CNM overall, CMM was paradoxically lower in obese women with SGA infants compared to non-obese women with SGA infants.
mod_finding: This study focuses on comparing neonatal and maternal morbidities in small for gestational age (SGA) versus appropriate for gestational age (AGA) infants born via repeat cesarean delivery and does not directly compare outcomes based on other modes of delivery.
